Dependency confusion is a type of supply-chain attack where an attacker exploits the way package managers resolve dependencies. In this attack, the attacker publishes a malicious package with the same name as a private package used by a target organization, but in a public repository. When the package manager resolves dependencies, it may mistakenly prioritize the public package over the private one due to naming conflicts, leading to the execution of malicious code. This attack takes advantage of the trust that developers place in package managers to fetch the correct dependencies. To mitigate this risk, organizations can use techniques like name mangling, where private packages are given unique names, or configure package managers to prioritize private repositories.
